content:
Phase 42 — Terminal.app session backend, implemented per the approved plan (round 2). Branch phase-42-terminal-backend, HEAD b1d9f59; diff vs plan approval (9ebe012): 16 files, +1772/-136.

What was built
- tagteam/terminal.py (new, 554 lines): the driver, same surface as iterm.py. create_session per §A.1 deterministic window accounting — cold launch reuses Terminal's own first (idle) window as Lead via `do script … in window id`, otherwise three untargeted `do script` windows; identification by window-id diff before/after each creation, exact-three invariant (created windows closed + no session file + False when `new` != 1); titles Lead/Watcher/Reviewer, placed side by side. session_id == tty (§A.2), window_id recorded for kill/list only. write_text_to_session, get_session_contents, session_id_is_valid, _any_session_alive, kill_session, list_sessions, adopt helpers, `_terminal_supported` platform gate, launch=True priming reuses session.wait_for_agent_ready.
- tagteam/tabs.py (new): .handoff-session.json helpers moved out of iterm.py (pure move, commit 0e35ad0; iterm.py re-exports) + `driver_for(project_dir)` dispatch on the file's `backend` field (missing → iterm2).
- session.py: SUPPORTED_BACKENDS += terminal; default_backend() iterm2 → tmux → terminal (macOS) → manual; `_validate_backend` off-macOS message; `session start --backend terminal`, `adopt --backend terminal`, `list-terminal`, `kill` via the driver.
- watcher.py: `--mode terminal`, auto-detected from the session file's `backend` (mismatch errors); send_tab_command / _capture_tail / watchdog probes go through the driver; iTerm2 path unchanged.
- server.py / state.py: dashboard log tail and `tagteam state` health lines resolve the driver from `backend`.
- cli.py, launch.py: wiring; docs/how-tagteam-works.md Terminal.app subsection; README + CITATION; version 3.6.0 (release commit fca365c, not tagged — tag after merge).

§A.3 empirical item — outcome (measured live 2026-08-17 against Claude Code + Codex, commit b1d9f59)
- The plan's two candidates (bare newline vs `& return`) both fail for Codex: Terminal delivers `do script` text as a paste, and Codex keeps pasted text — trailing newline included, even an explicit CR — in its composer. Claude Code submits on Terminal's own newline already.
- Shipped: two `do script`s in one AppleScript — the text, then after `delay 0.05` an empty `do script "" in tab i of w` (a lone newline). Claude: the extra newline on its now-empty input is a no-op (does not dismiss an open dialog); Codex: submits. Same text-then-Enter shape as iTerm2's `write text … newline NO` + CR. `_SUBMIT_SUFFIX` is gone (replaced by `_SUBMIT_DELAY_S`); recorded in the module docstring and docs/how-tagteam-works.md as the plan required.
- Two further live findings, same commit: (1) `_tab_script` now addresses the tab as `tab i of w` via an index loop — in AppleScript `contents of <loop-variable>` is the dereference operator, so `contents of t` returned the tab object, not screen text (probes were blind); (2) kill_session SIGHUPs the processes on each recorded tty (`pkill -HUP -t ttysNNN`) before `close … saving no`, because Terminal.app refuses to close a tab with running processes.

Verification
- tests/test_terminal.py (22) + tests/test_terminal_backend.py: FakeTerminal AppleScript stub covering plan §Tests (a)–(e) window accounting, titles, tty parse, session-file payload, write_text escaping + two-step submit ordering, contents tail, validity, kill (recorded ttys only, HUP order), list parsing, platform gating; session/watcher auto-detect/server/state dispatch tests.
- gate: see the gatekeeper entry on this round (on_submit) @ b1d9f59; pre-flight `gate check --skip-tests` passed.
- Live smoke on this Mac: session start/adopt/list-terminal/kill, watcher --mode terminal driving both agents.

GATE: PASS | scope 16 paths | plan-doc ok | tests ok (1345 passed, 5 skipped, 4m01s)
checked: HEAD b1d9f59

Approved. Implementation matches the approved Phase 42 plan: Terminal.app driver, session lifecycle/CLI dispatch, watcher auto-detection and mismatch handling, server/state health dispatch, docs, and empirical two-step submit behavior are all covered. Gate passed (1345 passed, 5 skipped); focused terminal tests pass (69 passed).
